issues: Non-blocking, fix before the next batch: the revert timer is 300s but the worst-case budget before pam-auth-update is timeout 120 (dpkg) + timeout 300 (apt) = 420s. If a first-time apt install is slow, the timer can fire and restore the stock stack mid-script. The script would then carry on, apply the new PAM stack, and have no timer left. This re-run is safe because both packages are already installed, so apt is skipped (SKIP-apt-already) and the only long step is dpkg at 120s at most. For later batches, either re-arm the timer after apt or add a check that the timer is still active before pam-auth-update. Alternatively, size the timer above the sum of the timeouts.

Non-blocking: PASTE 2 has to finish within 300s of TIMER-ARMED, not of OK-batch-9-pending. Any time spent in dpkg configure or pam-auth-update shrinks AJ's window. The .md says this, so keep the warning prominent.

Non-blocking: DEBCONF_NONINTERACTIVE_SEEN and DEBIAN_FRONTEND are exported, and the apt options use force-confdef and force-confold. Under set -e, a dpkg --configure -a timeout (exit 124) correctly takes the STOP-dpkg-configure path with revert and timer stop.
Non-blocking: the delivery and paste rules check out. Fenced pastes start with a '# RUNS ON:' line, the .sh is the single deliverable, Rollback is in the .md, and there is no reboot.

Non-blocking: all the STOP paths after arming now call systemctl stop on the timer, and the ERR/HUP trap does too. The revert script is idempotent and tolerates a pam-auth-update failure (WARN-pam-auth-update).
